memories.content: The user keeps a travel power bank in the first drawer beneath the desk.
The user packed three pairs of shoes for a two-night trip but wore only one pair.
For the next two-night trip, the user packed only one pair of walking shoes and reduced the bag's weight.
On a trip when the user forgot a charging cable, they bought a new one after arrival.
Before the next trip, the user checked charging items against a photo and packed all of them.
The user packed toiletries on the departure day and arrived 15 minutes late at the meeting place.
The next time, the user closed the bag the night before and departed on time.
The user's older sister considers it safer to pack an extra cable even for a short trip to avoid charging problems.
When creating a travel preparation list, confirm the trip length and actual activities with the user.
The local agent cannot establish what the next trip requires from the luggage used on the previous trip alone.
The user keeps four folding chairs for family barbecues in storage.
When six family members gathered in a noisy indoor restaurant, the user asked several times for the person across from them to repeat what was said.
The user held the next gathering in their father's yard and moved between seats while speaking with everyone.
On a day the user started the barbecue at midday, sunlight led them to finish the meal quickly.
The next time, the user started at 6 p.m. and remained outside until sunset.
Because the side dishes brought by the user's mother and older sister had no labels, the user opened the same container twice.
At the next gathering, the user wrote each food's name and who brought it on a small piece of paper.
After a barbecue, the user's younger brother prefers to divide leftover food into small containers to take home rather than discard it.
The local agent can summarize preparation and responses from prior family barbecues but cannot know the next attendees or weather.
The user's father's yard receives strong direct sunlight at midday; after 6 p.m., shade and wind lower the felt temperature.

analysis.overview: Both frames capture lessons from prior events and adjustments to later preparation, but in different domains: short-trip packing and family barbecues. Their shared planning principle is context-dependent; all other information is independently useful within its own domain, with no conflict or uncertainty.

relations.reason: The travel scope calls for confirming trip length and activities because prior luggage is insufficient, while the barbecue scope identifies attendees and weather as unknowable from previous gatherings.
relations.summary: Planning the next event requires current event-specific facts rather than relying on prior-event evidence alone.
